name: The Feature-Trace Checker
oneLiner: Drives the app in a real browser, enables the function-call trace toggle, sends a prompt, and asserts the answer, its trace, and the saved conversation all appear.
lead: Runs the actual app in a headless-or-headed Chromium session via Playwright, exactly as a user would — clicking, typing, waiting. It first flips the settings toggle that surfaces the app's function-call trace, sends a prompt, waits for the streamed answer to fully settle, then asserts the trace panel rendered and the conversation persisted to history.
chore: Checking this by hand is tedious and easy to rush: open settings, find the toggle, set it to Yes, save, start a new chat, type the prompt, then — the slow part — watch until the streamed answer stops growing (minutes), squint for the function-call panel, note the title, go home, and scroll the list to confirm the conversation saved. Across many prompts it's mind-numbing, and a distracted tester calls a half-streamed answer 'done'.
instead: The agent runs the full click-by-click routine and, critically, waits for the answer to truly finish streaming before asserting. Per prompt it records answer length, whether the trace panel appeared, the conversation title, and whether the conversation showed up in the saved list — then returns a clean pass/fail summary.
whyItMatters: A human watching a screen eventually blinks, gets bored, or calls a still-streaming answer finished — the agent never does, so slow or missing function-call traces get caught instead of waved through.

howItWorks.step: Launches Chromium, reusing a saved storage-state session if one exists, otherwise pausing up to three minutes for a one-time manual sign-in.
howItWorks.explain: The auth model is **cache-if-present, sign-in-once-if-not**: the spread `...(fs.existsSync(AUTH_FILE) ? { storageState: AUTH_FILE } : {})` conditionally injects the saved cookies/tokens, so a returning run is authenticated silently and a first run gets a clean context. Login is detected by **URL sniffing** — if the app bounced the browser to `login.microsoftonline`/`login.live.com`, a human is given up to 180s to complete SSO (including MFA), after which `storageState({ path: AUTH_FILE })` **persists the session so it never asks again**. The `goto` is wrapped in `.catch(() => {})` because `networkidle` on an app with background polling can legitimately time out — swallowing it lets the very next line inspect the real URL rather than crashing on a non-fatal navigation timeout. `headless: !args.headed` means headed is opt-in, which matters precisely for that first manual sign-in.

howItWorks.step: Navigates settings and flips the function-call-modifier toggle to Yes, then submits — only changing it if it isn't already Yes, and falling back to a human if the menu markup shifted.
howItWorks.explain: The toggle is set **read-before-write**: it reads `currentVal` and only opens the dropdown and picks 'Yes' when the value isn't already 'Yes', so a re-run doesn't needlessly re-toggle and risk flipping a setting that's already correct. The comparison is defensively normalized (`?.trim().toLowerCase()`) so stray whitespace or casing in the rendered label can't cause a false 'not yes'. Locators are chosen for **resilience to markup drift**: the container is pinned by the stable `.test-FunctionCallModifiers` test hook, but the caret and the 'Yes' option each supply **two selector alternatives** (`.k-input-button, button[aria-label="Select"]` and `.k-list-item…, li…`) so a component-library class rename doesn't break the click. The final submit uses `click({ force: true })` to bypass Playwright's actionability checks — deliberate, because an overlay or animation shouldn't block a button the agent knows is there.

howItWorks.step: Per prompt: starts a new chat, waits for the prompt box to become editable, types the prompt, and submits.
howItWorks.explain: The prompt box is disabled while the app initializes, so typing into it too early would silently drop characters — this **polls until it's genuinely typeable** rather than guessing with a fixed sleep. Editability requires **both** signals to clear: `aria-readonly !== 'true'` AND the native `readonly` attribute being absent (`=== null`), because the app can toggle either one independently. Every `getAttribute` is `.catch`-guarded to a **pessimistic default** (`'true'` / a truthy readonly) so a transient DOM detach during a re-render reads as 'still locked' and keeps waiting instead of falsely declaring success. On timeout it escalates through a two-stage recovery — a `force`-click to jolt focus, then a full page reload — before returning `false`, so a truly stuck box is reported rather than hung on forever.

howItWorks.step: Watches the streaming answer and only proceeds once its HTML has held byte-for-byte identical across 30 consecutive checks — its stability signal that the answer is complete, not merely paused.
howItWorks.explain: This is the agent's headline capability: it distinguishes a **finished** answer from a merely **paused** one, which a human watcher can't reliably do. It compares `innerHTML` **byte-for-byte** — not text, and not just length — so even a late-arriving citation chip or formatting change resets stability; and it demands **30 consecutive unchanged reads at 2s each = ~60s of true silence** before declaring done, deliberately long because streamed LLM output stalls mid-answer for many seconds. `curHTML.length > 0` is a required guard so an empty read (element momentarily detached) can never be mistaken for a stable answer, and **any** change resets `stableCount` to 0, so the 60s window must be clean end-to-end. The whole thing is bounded by a 5-minute deadline so a never-completing answer eventually returns what it has rather than hanging the batch; `.catch(() => '')` on every read keeps a transient locator error from aborting the wait.

howItWorks.step: Asserts the function-call panel rendered, captures the conversation title, navigates home, and polls the saved-conversations list up to 45s for a title match.
howItWorks.explain: Three assertions in sequence, each written to record a **negative result rather than crash**: the trace presence and title reads both use `isVisible(...).catch(() => false)` so a missing panel logs as 'not found' instead of throwing and losing the whole prompt's result. The persistence check is the interesting one — after navigating home it **polls the saved-list for up to 45s** because save-to-history is asynchronous and the conversation often isn't there the instant you arrive. Matching is a **case-insensitive prefix contains** on the first 30 chars of the title (`slice(0, 30)`), deliberately loose because the panel can truncate or lightly reformat the displayed title versus the header `h2`. It re-queries `panelItems` and its `count` **every iteration** so newly-arrived list entries are seen, and breaks the instant a match is found; if 45s elapses with no hit, `foundInPanel` stays false and that becomes the reportable save-bug signal.

howItWorks.step: Repeats for every prompt, then prints a summary and writes the JSON report, recovering on its own if one prompt throws.
howItWorks.explain: One JSON report captures the whole batch, and the filename is built to be **filesystem-safe and non-colliding**: `toISOString()` has its `:` and `.` replaced (illegal or awkward in filenames on some OSes) and is sliced to second precision, then tagged with `env` so a dev and a qa run never overwrite each other. `mkdirSync(..., { recursive: true })` creates the full report path idempotently on a fresh checkout. The `results` array — every prompt's answer length, trace-found flag, title, and persisted flag — is written **verbatim** so a failing prompt (missing trace, `not found in panel`) is preserved for a human to chase later, not just summarized.

examples.caption: A prompt that should trigger a function call
examples.input: The prompt 'What does the firm do for expense reports?' with the trace toggle enabled.
examples.output: The answer finishes rendering, the function-call panel is detected, the title is captured, and the conversation is confirmed present in the saved list — recorded as a pass with the word count and trace noted.

examples.caption: A batch run from a file
examples.input: A file of five prompts run in sequence.
examples.output: Five conversations driven start to finish; the summary shows, e.g., '5 answered, 4 with a function-call trace, 5 saved to the list, 0 errors.'

examples.caption: The conversation never persists
examples.input: A prompt whose answer completes normally but whose conversation doesn't appear in the saved list within the 45s window.
examples.output: The answer and trace are recorded, but the conversation is flagged 'not found in panel after 45s' — a clear save-or-refresh bug signal for a human to chase.

underHood.heading: Launches Chromium and signs in
underHood.input: A saved storage-state session file, if one exists.
underHood.output: A Chromium session logged into the app — or a 3-minute pause for a one-time manual sign-in.

underHood.heading: Enables the function-call toggle
underHood.output: The function-call modifier set to Yes and submitted, so every answer from now can surface its trace.

underHood.heading: Submits the prompt like a user
underHood.whenRuns: Once per prompt in your list.
underHood.output: A new chat started, the prompt typed and Enter pressed — only once the box is confirmed editable.

underHood.heading: Waits for the stream to settle
underHood.whenRuns: Right after the prompt is sent.
underHood.input: The streaming answer HTML on screen.
underHood.output: The complete answer — the agent only proceeds once the HTML holds identical for 60s straight, so it never asserts on a half-streamed answer.

underHood.heading: Asserts trace, title, and persistence
underHood.whenRuns: After each answer is confirmed complete.
underHood.output: Whether the function-call panel rendered, the conversation title, and — after navigating home — whether the conversation appears in the saved list.

underHood.heading: Writes the final report
underHood.whenRuns: After every prompt in the batch has run.
underHood.input: The pass/fail result of every prompt.
underHood.output: One timestamped JSON file plus a printed summary — how many answered, how many showed a trace, how many persisted.

prerequisites: Node ≥ 18 and a terminal (macOS/Linux shell or Windows PowerShell).
Playwright installed with its Chromium binary downloaded (`npx playwright install`).
A real account for the app — the first run pauses up to 3 minutes for a one-time manual sign-in, then reuses the saved storage-state session.
The app must expose a settings toggle that surfaces its function-call trace — the agent finds and enables it for you.

steps.label: Install Node.js — the runtime the agent runs on.
steps.cmd:
# macOS (with Homebrew):
brew install node

# or download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, then check it worked:
node -v   # should print v18 or higher
steps.why: The agent is a TypeScript program; Node executes it. Install once per machine.
steps.firstRun: Only needed on a fresh machine.

steps.label: Install dependencies and the Chromium binary.
steps.cmd:
cd path/to/the-agents
npm install
npx playwright install   # one-time: downloads the actual browser binary
steps.why: `npm install` pulls the agent's dependencies; `playwright install` downloads the Chromium binary the agent drives — a one-time download, not a per-run step.
steps.firstRun: Downloads Chromium (a few minutes on a slow connection).
steps.rerun: Skipped entirely once the binary is present.

steps.label: Run once headed to sign in.
steps.cmd:
npx tsx agents/function-call-share-agent.ts --env dev \
  --prompt "What does the app do for expense reports?"
steps.why: Omitting `--headless` opens a visible Chromium window. The first run pauses on the SSO screen for manual login, then persists the storage-state session so it never asks again.
steps.firstRun: Pauses up to 3 minutes for manual sign-in, then saves the session to a local file.
steps.rerun: Signs in silently from the saved session — no pause, unless it expired.

steps.label: Run for real on a prompt list, headless if you like.
steps.why: `--input` reads one prompt per line and runs the full click-type-wait-assert routine for each. `--headless` drops the window once you trust it — useful in CI.

steps.label: Open the report.
steps.why: Per prompt, records whether the trace appeared, the answer's word count, the conversation title, and whether it persisted to the saved-conversations list.

inputs.name: --prompt "..." (repeatable) or --input <file>
inputs.desc: One or more prompts to send, typed directly or read one-per-line from a text file.

inputs.name: --env dev|qa
inputs.desc: Which environment's app instance to drive in the browser.

inputs.name: --headless
inputs.desc: Run with no visible window (default is headed, so you can watch and sign in the first time).

outputs.name: console log
outputs.desc: A numbered step trace per prompt as it happens — new chat, prompt sent, response complete, trace checked, saved-list checked.

outputs.name: FuncCallShare_<env>_<timestamp>.json
outputs.desc: One pass/fail record per prompt — answer word count, whether the function-call trace rendered, the conversation title, and whether it persisted to the saved list.

runbook.rerun: Sign-in is cached via the storage-state file, so re-runs skip straight to sending prompts. Everything else is fully live — each run starts a brand-new chat per prompt, so re-running the same list produces a fresh batch to check, not a replay.
runbook.integrate: Built for a regression suite: point it at a fixed prompt list after any change that could touch the trace feature or the save-to-history path, run it headless in CI, and fail the build on any 'not found in panel' or missing-trace result — exactly the intermittent bug a rushed human waves through because they blinked at the wrong moment.

video.caption: A 3-4 minute screen recording: a real browser drives itself through the app and checks the trace shows up.
script: Open a terminal and say: 'This agent drives the real app in a browser and checks a hidden trace appears. Watch.'
Run `node -v` and mention `npx playwright install` was already done to download the browser.
Run the headed command; show the actual Chrome window pop open.
Point out the one-time sign-in pause (or skip it and say 'this only happens once — after that it's saved').
Narrate as the settings toggle gets switched to reveal the behind-the-scenes trace.
Show the prompt getting typed into the box and Enter pressed.
Let the answer stream, then say: 'It won't move on until the text has stayed perfectly still for a full minute — that's how it knows the answer is really done, not just paused.'
Point at the trace panel appearing on screen once the answer finishes.
Show it navigating home and scrolling the saved-conversations list to confirm the new chat is really there.
Open the saved `.json`; show the pass/fail fields for that one run.
Close: 'Run this headless in CI on every prompt list, and a missing trace fails the build instead of slipping past a bored tester.'
